```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

_ = torch.manual_seed(481)
digits = pd.read_csv("data/optdigits-test.csv", header=None)
x = torch.tensor(digits.iloc[:, :64].to_numpy(), dtype=torch.float32) / 16
y = torch.tensor(digits[64].to_numpy())
n_train = 1200
order = torch.randperm(len(x))
x_train, y_train = x[order[:n_train]], y[order[:n_train]]
x_test, y_test = x[order[n_train:]], y[order[n_train:]]
n_test = len(x_test)
print(x_train.shape, x_test.shape)
```

The exercises use the `r format(nrow(py$digits), big.mark = ",")` handwritten digits from the [course overview](course-overview.qmd),
from the same local copy, [`data/optdigits-test.csv`](data/optdigits-test.csv),
of the UCI Machine Learning Repository's data [@alpaydin1998optdigits]. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
Each image's 64 pixels, from 0 to 16, are divided by 16 so that they run from 0 to 1,
and a random `r format(py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` images form a [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set),
with the other images as a [test set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-test-set).
